# Aurora Station Operations Handbook

## Station Overview

Aurora Station is the shore facility that supports the Aurora buoy network in the
northern fjord. The station houses the wet lab, the instrument workshop, the data
room and a small crew dormitory. Day-to-day operations are run by a station lead
and two rotating instrument technicians on four-week shifts.

## Power Systems

The station runs on a grid connection backed by two diesel generators. Generator A
starts automatically within twelve seconds of a grid outage; generator B is started
by hand only when generator A has been running for more than six hours. Fuel for
both generators is stored in a double-walled tank behind the workshop.

## Buoy Maintenance

Each buoy is recovered by the workboat Kittiwake twice a year, in April and in
October. Recovery crews replace the mooring shackles, scrape biofouling from the
hull, and swap the lithium battery packs. A buoy that misses two consecutive
telemetry windows is scheduled for an unplanned recovery within ten days.

## Data Retention

Raw hydrophone audio is kept on the station archive server for ninety days and is
then deleted. Processed acoustic summaries are retained indefinitely and are
replicated nightly to the university mirror in Tromsø. Telemetry logs older than
two years are compressed and moved to cold storage tapes.

## Emergency Evacuation

In an evacuation the station lead sounds the long horn three times. Crew muster at
the boathouse slipway and take the headcount board with them. If the slipway is
blocked by ice, the secondary muster point is the helicopter pad above the
generator shed.

## Radio Schedule

The station checks in with the regional coast guard on VHF channel 16 at 06:00 and
18:00 every day. Weather reports from the buoy network are read out on channel 12
immediately after the evening check-in.
